text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed a p99 spike on token-level latency in eu-west during the 02:30-03:15 window. TTFT p99 jumped ~300ms, p50 steady. tokens/sec didn't change. Filing a quick drill here so oncall can triage.

maria: Link to the grafana panel? Is this correlated with batch window or autoscaler events?

alex: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abcd/token-latency?orgId=1&var-region=eu-west — looks like tail only and aligns with a few bursts of cold-starts. Also seeing slight drop in kv_cache_hit_ratio.

jin: Query I used to eyeball tail:
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,model,region))
```
And cache hit query: `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups_total[5m]))` by (pool) — hit ratio dipped ~8% on the same window.

caroline: Noted — we rolled kernel patch 2024-11-10 to the dedicated nodes in eu-west around 02:10 via the ops play. ops-bot shows the rollout, maybe NIC drivers got a change. Could be interrupt storm causing tail latencies on certain shards.

ops-bot: Deploy summary: rollout kernel-5.18.12-nic-fix to pool-dedicated-eu-west at 2024-11-10T02:12Z. 48/48 nodes updated. No automated rollback. :information_source:

sam: If it's driver/NIC related, we should broaden the drill: check dmesg/syslogs for RX/TX errors and CPU steal on the inference pods' nodes. Also tune the alert to avoid noisy single-minute spikes — prefer 15m sustained p99 above threshold. Proposed alert rule snippet:
```yaml
- alert: TokenLatencyHighP99_Sustained
  expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region)) > 0.8
  for: 15m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "Sustained high p99 token latency in {{ $labels.region }}"
```

maria: Good call. Also suggest adding a panel for `kv_cache_warmup_ratio` and `kv_cache_evictions` so we can see if cold starts are driving tail. Example query for warmup ratio: `sum(kv_cache_warmed_items) / sum(kv_cache_capacity)` by (pool).

jin: I checked the node metrics quickly — small spikes in softirq and irq handled counts around the same times on 3 nodes, and one node had a transient increase in `kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total` for the kvcache sidecar. Posting logs to the incident thread.

alex: Action items: 1) ops to validate NIC driver telemetry and consider rollback for that pool if we see repeat events. 2) Devex/product to add kvcache warm/cold metrics to the SLO dashboard. 3) SRE to change alert to 15m sustained and add runbook section for kernel rollouts. I'll file a follow-up ticket and assign.

caroline: I'll open the rollback ticket and tag @ops-eng. If we confirm kernel is culprit we should snapshot core dumps and escalate to vendor.

maria: Thanks — added the dashboard request to #obs-kanban. Also turning the alert into a warning for now while we gather repeatability so we don't page for noise. :thumbsup:

alex: Great. If anyone sees a reoccurrence ping here immediately and attach `node-exporter` and `dmesg` snippets.
